security_spec.violation_condition: kernel or hypervisor code writes RRIDSCP.op to stall/unstall an RRID that is marked rridscp_unselectable[rrid]=1 by hardware, then proceeds without checking that RRIDSCP.stat != 3, silently assuming the operation took effect
security_spec.summary: RRIDSCP writes to unselectable RRIDs now set stat=3 and are silently ignored; kernel/firmware callers must check stat post-write or risk operating on the wrong transaction state (unstall silently failing → permanent DoS; stall silently failing → unauthorized DMA proceeds)

location.file_path: N/A (no IOPMP driver in Linux kernel)

findings.finding: The Linux kernel (arch/riscv and drivers/) contains no IOPMP driver. There is no code that writes RRIDSCP, MDSTALL, MDSTALLH, or implements the stall/unstall/resume programming sequence described in the RISC-V IOPMP specification. Consequently, the RRIDSCP vulnerability pattern — where software writes RRIDSCP.op to stall/unstall an RRID marked rridscp_unselectable[rrid]=1 by hardware, then proceeds without checking RRIDSCP.stat != 3 — cannot manifest because no such code exists. The only 'iopmp' references found in the tree are clock gate definitions (CLK_IOPMP_*) in drivers/clk/thead/clk-th1520-ap.c, which gate clocks to an IOPMP hardware block on the T-Head TH1520 SoC but do not interact with IOPMP registers.

spec_citations.excerpt: After MDSTALL and all RRIDSCP are written, the action to stall desired transactions may not take effect immediately ... Step 1.3: write RRIDSCP zero or more times; Step 1.4: poll until MDSTALL.is_busy == 0
RRIDSCP: stat[31:30] — 0: not implemented, 1: stalled, 2: not stalled, 3: unimplemented or unselectable RRID
